title: CAAC skill workflows
summary: Start with a CAAC skill to write or review a contract, or implement a reviewed clause. The review skill can run local MCP lint. The CLI also supports authoring and package verification.

features.result: A reviewable draft with open decisions and verification results.

features.request: Review an existing draft or package.
features.result: A review disposition, cited findings, and owner decisions.

features.request: Implement a reviewed clause with independent candidates.
features.result: A selected implementation with a recorded comparison and replay evidence.

implementation_roles.responsibility: Pin the clause and cases. Sketch the interface, mock output, and critical pseudocode.
Build the same task in separate workspaces from the same reviewed inputs.
Challenge the mock first. Replay both completed candidates against the same acceptance cases.
Select a base from the review, incorporate justified changes, and rerun the checks on the final code.
Resolve open contract policy and approve the exact revision when ready.

mcp_review.scope: Start the installed binary with `caac mcp` as a local stdio server. Use `caac_lint` to check the syntax and case references of selected Markdown. The CLI and MCP share the same Rust checks.
mcp_review.input: Send scope as `complete`, `partial`, or `unknown`. Send an ordered `documents` array with one to eight objects containing `name` and `markdown`. Each name must be unique and contain one to 128 Unicode scalar values with at least one non-whitespace character. Each document can contain up to 256 KiB of UTF-8 Markdown. The name is a display label. The stdio transport discards malformed JSON frames and lines over 16 MiB.
mcp_review.result: The structured result echoes the caller-declared scope and includes the SHA-256 of each document, lint status, diagnostics, and `semantic_review: pending`. A broken reference produces `lint: failed`. Invalid tool arguments produce a tool error. The tool reads and checks the supplied text in memory.
mcp_review.verification: Run `cargo test --locked --test mcp` to replay initialization, discovery, valid and invalid inputs, cross-document references, CLI parity, and the maximum escaped input. Register the local command in your MCP client. In Codex, run `codex mcp add caac -- caac mcp`. Use an absolute path to the installed binary if the client cannot resolve `caac`.
mcp_review.follow_up: Candidate verification and clause tracing remain available through the CLI. To assess coverage, the review skill needs an approved obligation list and an explicit review scope.
